newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin sets limits for Russia regional Eurobonds.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin sets limits for Russia regional Eurobonds.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin has issued a decree on terms for Eurobonds planned by the Moscow and St Petersburg municipal governments and the Nizhny Novgorod region, the presidential press service said on Wednesday.

The decree, signed late on Tuesday and effective immediately, limits total debt issue by those governments to 30 percent of their revenues, excluding loans, and limits total debt service charges to 15 percent of non-debt revenues.

The local governments must obtain two international credit ratings and get permission from the Russian Central Bank before they can issue the bonds, which would be subject to double-taxation treaties, a press service statement said.
The decree did not set conditions under which other regional authorities could issue Eurobonds.
Nizhny Novgorod region and Moscow have received ratings of Ba2 from Moody's and BB- from Standard & Poor. Last year Russia was assigned the same ratings for its soveriegn Eurobond.

Moscow plans to issue up to $500 million in three- or five-year bonds, St Petersburg wants to issue about $300 million in two- to five-year bonds while Nizhny Novgorod is aiming at up to $100 million in bonds with a five-year maturity.

Some bond issues have been delayed due to a lack of clarity in regulations, although the government has said regional Eurobonds would not be subject to a 15 percent tax on government securities and a proposed 0.8 percent registration fee.

Other regions considering or planning Eurobonds include the Republic of Tatarstan in central European Russia, and the regions of Irkutsk in Siberia, Sverdlovsk in the Urals and Leningrad surrounding St Petersburg.
